science.title: An incommensurate ultra-low fractional-order Chen system for sliding mode synchronization and secure communication
science.description: This study investigates the dynamical characteristics, synchronization properties, and secure communication capability of an incommensurate fractional-order Chen (IFOC) chaotic system. A key contribution of this work is the identification and utilization of extremely low fractional-order values ($$q_1$$ = 0.2, $$q_2$$ = 0.3, $$q_3$$ = 0.4), close to the critical threshold at which chaotic dynamics vanish. In these regimes, the chaotic bandwidth becomes significantly compressed, and numerical simulation becomes highly challenging due to increased memory effects and reduced Lyapunov divergence. Despite this difficulty, the system is shown to exhibit a persistent chaotic attractor. To provide a transparent synchronization baseline under these chaotic conditions, a conventional full-state active sliding-mode controller with model-based cancellation is adopted, and its nominal closed-loop stability is established through a component-wise vector-Lyapunov framework formulated for incommensurate fractional-order systems. Building on the resulting synchronized dynamics, a projective multiplexed chaotic masking scheme is designed to transmit multiple messages securely. Simulation results demonstrate accurate message recovery, strong masking capability, and high resilience to parameter mismatch, noise, and controller gain perturbation. The ability to achieve secure communication at such low fractional orders distinguishes this work from existing literature and highlights the potential of fractional-order systems in advanced secure communication frameworks.

science.title: Fractional-order modeling of paliperidone inhibition in RAGE-HMGB1 signaling dynamics via a hyperbolic tangent sigmoid deep neural network
science.description: The HMGB1–RAGE signaling axis is a key inflammatory pathway associated with cancer cell survival, proliferation, invasion, and treatment resistance. Classical integer-order models may not adequately describe delayed receptor trafficking, persistent intracellular signaling, and memory-dependent cellular responses. In this work, we develop an exploratory in silico framework that combines a Caputo fractional-order model with a hyperbolic tangent sigmoid deep neural network (HTS–DNN) to study the potential inhibitory effect of Paliperidone on HMGB1–RAGE dynamics. The model describes free RAGE receptors, HMGB1–RAGE and Paliperidone–RAGE complexes, downstream signaling, viable cells, apoptosis, and drug concentration. The biological consistency of the model is supported through existence, uniqueness, positivity, and boundedness results. Reference solutions are generated using a fractional Adams–Bashforth–Moulton predictor–corrector scheme for HMGB1-only, Paliperidone-only, and combined exposure cases, and are then used to train the HTS–DNN through the Levenberg–Marquardt (LM) algorithm. Numerical results show that the model accurately reproduces the fractional dynamics with low prediction errors. The simulations suggest that Paliperidone-related receptor occupancy may suppress RAGE-mediated signaling, reduce cell viability, and increase apoptosis-related responses. Fractional orders $$\alpha <1$$ produce slower relaxation and persistent transient behavior compared with $$\alpha =1$$, emphasizing the role of memory effects. Since no direct fitting to experimental time-series data is performed, the results should be interpreted as qualitative mechanistic predictions and as a computational platform for future calibration and validation.

science.title: Codification and description of growth stages in guava (Psidium guajava L.) using the extended BBCH scale
science.description: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in extending the production calendar for guava (Psidium guajava L.) by cultivating it outside traditional growing areas. Since guava is very sensitive to environmental factors, such efforts often disrupt the regularity of cropping due to changes in phenological patterns. The lack of an universally accepted and standardized phenological scale for guava represents a significant limitation for an accurate description and comparative analysis of its developmental stages. In the present study, the flowering development of guava was characterised systematically and placed in context with the BBCH scale of Biologische Bundesanstalt, Bundessortenamt, and Chemische Industrie. For this objective, phenological development of Lucknow-49 guava variety was recorded over two consecutive years. The observations regarding phenology were precisely matched with the BBCH coding system thereby allowing the integration of floral developmental stages within its major growth stage classes. Standardization in methodology in this regard provides a strong, consistent framework that allows better comparability and reproducibility of results in the phenology of guava.

science.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of tea cultivar Fuding Dahao
science.description: Tea (Camellia sinensis) is a globally important economic crop. Among elite cultivars, ‘Fuding Dahao’ is particularly prized for its superior agronomic traits and its central role in premium white tea production. However, the lack of a high-quality chromosome-level genome for this regionally adapted cultivar has hindered molecular breeding efforts. Here, we present the first chromosome-level reference genome of ‘Fuding Dahao’ assembled using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C chromatin interaction mapping. The final 3.30 Gb assembly is highly contiguous, with 90% of the sequences anchored to 15 pseudochromosomes. A total of 54,345 protein-coding genes were predicted, representing a substantial improvement in both assembly contiguity and annotation completeness compared with previously published tea genomes. This high quality genome provides a critical resource for dissecting the genetic basis of white tea quality traits and accelerating molecular breeding programs. Our results fill a major gap in tea genomics and lay a solid foundation for the development of superior, locally adapted tea cultivars.

ai.title: Careers are no longer linear. UWA's global MBA with IIMK Certificate is helping managers step into the global market
ai.description: New Delhi [India], August 8: The global economy today houses a highly competitive labour market. Over 52% of professionals globally are seeking new roles, yet nearly 80% feel unprepared to navigate the job market due to skills gaps and uncertainty about standing out. The same 2026 LinkedIn Research report states that professionals are changing roles and industries more frequently than ever, reflecting a move towards more fluid, non-linear careers. In this context, the idea of a fixed "career path" is quietly disappearing. As AI and automation continue to reshape work, the shelf life of specialised expertise is shrinking. What endures is something more fundamental: the ability to think strategically, make sound decisions under uncertainty, and lead across contexts. Career progression is no longer defined by where you start, but by how well you adapt.
